# Independent audit of the arbitrary-contact diffuse-curvature stress theorem

Audited `candidate c7a0c159c6cf35f0`, together with its
potential-locality and direct-budget separation dependencies. The theorem
passes under the stated attained-local-minimum and finite-cover assumptions.
No numerical OC conclusion follows merely from this audit.

1. A proper line meets a planar convex boundary in at most two points.
   The normal cone of either point has zero curvature measure on its
   interior, and only point atoms can occur at its endpoints. A supporting
   facet adds a single atom normal. Hence each cap-crossing normal set is
   null for that fiber's diffuse curvature. On a source stratum where
   r_z>0, its R_z^c-null subsets are R-null; this correctly transfers the
   assertion to the common measure while retaining only affected fibers.
2. Outside those bad normals the complete exposed face has a strict cap
   sign. Upper semicontinuity of support faces makes this sign uniform in
   a neighborhood. This supplies the exact cap guard for source-supported
   variations, including nearby possible facet normals.
3. The zero-set identity for a Jensen gap follows from BV locality. A
   Lipschitz gap whose derivative is BV is differentiable outside the
   derivative's countably many jumps. At a nonnegative zero its derivative
   is zero. The diffuse derivative of that BV derivative vanishes on its
   zero level set. The g dtheta term vanishes too. Thus every actual density
   vector satisfies the active zero-pattern rows almost everywhere.
4. On a guarded source pattern, v lies in the kernels of precisely those
   rows that are zero on the source. The variation of such a gap is
   identically zero on the WHOLE guard, not merely on the source set.
   All other gaps have a uniform positive margin there. This is the crucial
   exact feasibility argument that removes stable-contact assumptions.
5. Each source is dominated by all affected fiber curvature measures, so
   bounded source densities preserve convexity in both parameter signs.
   The two sine/cosine moments make its potential and first derivative zero
   off the compact interval. Additional finite first-area orthogonality
   equations leave nonzero sources available and make every first mass zero.
6. Every finite list of generators can be placed on disjoint subintervals
   within its guards, because the source measures are nonatomic. Cross
   area terms then vanish exactly. No infinite perturbation or common
   small-parameter bound is required.
7. Using the FULL finite feature vector (M',F_1',...,F_N') correctly retains
   all first-order cap information when indicator patterns vary by guard.
   Its image has a finite basis of actual feasible tests. The direct-budget
   epigraph cone can therefore be separated once globally. The exact signed
   joint homotheties give the positive objective multiplier and normalization
   sum lambda=1/beta even at cap/facet coincidences.
8. The same separator annihilates every acceleration feature from every
   source. Potential locality turns this into a diffuse measure identity
   on each source support. A finite kernel basis and countable source
   exhaustion give simultaneous almost-everywhere nullspace identities.
   Thus the multiplier is indeed one common lambda, not a patternwise choice.

Useful wording clarification: define I_jz as the strict exposed-face sign
at every good angle, including atoms; only assign arbitrary values where
the exposed face meets the cap line. The first-mass features integrate
against the FULL curvature measure R_z. Any admissible variation is zero
near the bad cap-crossing faces of its affected coordinates, so these
arbitrary values never affect a feature. This reconciles those integrals
with the final diffuse-only conclusion.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
